summary: This is a sound stage 4 that removes the 1.4 us _pre_attention_kernel at full decode B=1, and its in-process interleaved gate already gives an A/B. Two parts of the spec need fixing before the build: it claims about 2.6 us of node gap that the profiles do not show, and it asks for RoPE, which full layers do not use.
justification: Mechanism: at full decode_1 the shape is 22.6 us. The kernels are splitkv_attn_sk_kernel<4,true,true> at 18.6 us and _pre_attention_kernel at 1.4 us. Folding the pre-attention work into the stream-K kernel removes one graph node. The ownership argument holds: tile ranges are disjoint and key seq-1 is cache_loc[b], so exactly one CTA owns the new K/V row. The per-CTA q build is redundant but cheap in bytes (132 x 2 KB of L2). WEAKEST LINK, in two parts. (1) The gain is overstated. The spec attributes ~2.6 us of the row to 'the second graph node and its launch gap'. But sliding decode_1 runs ONE kernel and shows the same residual: 13.1 us shape vs 10.2 us kernel, 2.9 us. So the residual comes from each graph replay, not from each node (the judge already subtracts ~4 us of fixed replay cost). PDL from pre-attention also did not move decode_1 (23.08 vs 22.6 us), which fits that reading. The 7.2 us B=32 saving cited for s3-fused-preattn is not in its result either: shape 223.1 vs master 226.4 us, about 3.3 us, and at B=16 109.6 vs 111.1 us, about 1.5 us, with the fused kernel itself growing (the spec's own risk note says +3.1 us of build at B=16). Realistic ceiling: about 1.4 us, minus whatever the q build adds to the critical path. That gives roughly 21.2-21.8 us against the stated target of <=21 us, which needs everything to go right. Floor is 4.3 us, so M3 (<=1.5x floor) is out of reach and is not what this stage is for. (2) Latency of the q build. At B=1 every CTA has very little work (80K keys / 132 CTAs, about 9-10 tiles of 64). So a serialized load of qkv, then RMSNorm, then the FP8 cast before the first QK could add 0.5-1 us to every CTA and erase the saving. The s3 review already flagged this, and sliding-fused-hoist-first-tile showed that prologue ordering is fragile here. Build it so the first KV tiles' cp.async are issued BEFORE the q build, and the 2 KB qkv slice rides the ring with the first tile. SPEC ERROR: the change says 'RMSNorm + interleaved RoPE' for q and 'norm+rope K'. Full layers have NO RoPE (TASK.md lines 18/29; master full-layer pre-attention runs with ROPE=False). Mirror master: scaleless RMSNorm, eps 1e-5, then the e4m3 cast, no rotation. Otherwise the bit-exact cache self-check fails and correctness falls back. Expected directions are consistent: full decode_1 (weight 16) faster, decode_16/32 and sliding flat. The headline effect is about 16 x 1.4 / 2608 = 0.9%, inside the CI, which is acceptable for a rewrite judged on kernel time.
confounders: full-decode1-streamk-s3-two-level-ticket: this is the incumbent kernel the change modifies, not an independent confounder. The prepare-time interleaved graph-replay gate ([fused two-level] vs [pre-attn + two-level]) is already an in-process A/B against it.

fused-preattention-triton (plus paired-heads-launch-cleanup and its ab-tune batch gate): the fused prologue must reproduce master's B=1 pre-attention output exactly. At B=1 the paired predicate (batch > 1) is false, so q uses the unpaired layout that the two-level kernel reads today. The bit-exact cache-row check covers K/V, but q's smem layout and scale must also match what splitkv_attn_sk_kernel<4,true,true> consumes.

full-decode-splitkv-s3-fused-preattn (depends_on, not landed, within-ci): FUSED_PRE was written against the s2 single-level splitkv_attn_sk_fused_kernel, not master's <4,true,true> template. Porting it is a merge, not a flag flip. Its measured net saving (about 1.5 us at B=16, about 3.3 us at B=32) is the honest prior, not 7.2 us.
full-decode1-sk-pdl-from-preattn: a null PDL result at decode_1 suggests there is little inter-node gap to recover. That caps this change at about the pre-attention kernel's own 1.4 us.
interference: No companions. This is a rewrite stage gated by an in-process interleaved graph-replay A/B against exactly the path it replaces, with PATH CHOSEN printing both numbers. That alone makes a gain, a loss or a fallback readable from one run. The only overlapping landed change is the incumbent itself. Reverting the pre-attention or pairing landings would just break the comparison. With 8 checks and 8 queued hypotheses, a companion would buy nothing that the printed gate numbers do not already give.
rules_flags: Not a rules problem but a correctness one: no RoPE on full layers. Drop the rotation the spec mentions, or the cache rows and output will differ from the reference.

Last-tile owner: if it both stores the new K/V row to the cache and its tile gather reads that row back through cp.async from global memory, there is an intra-CTA race. Either use the register/smem copy for key seq-1 as specified and gather only keys < seq-1, or store, then __threadfence_block/__syncthreads, then issue that tile.

The cache write happens inside the timed kernel and depends only on that call's inputs. That is allowed (store_cache is part of kernel_fn). Keep the two-state rule: no static pointer into a state's cache. The self-resetting ticket arrays are fine.
q stays at FP8 E4M3 or wider; RMSNorm, softmax and the merges stay in fp32. Every key is attended, including seq-1 from the fused row.
open_questions: Where does the ~2.6-2.9 us shape-vs-kernel residual at B=1 come from, given that a single-kernel shape (sliding decode_1) shows the same amount? If it is per-graph cost, this stage's ceiling is about 1.4 us, and the next decode_1 lever is inside the kernel's 18.6 us (0.89 TB/s vs about 4.8 TB/s): more bytes in flight per CTA and the cost of the two-level merge tail.

Does the q build overlap the first tiles' cp.async prologue? Print the eager per-kernel time of the fused kernel vs <4,true,true> in prepare, so the q-build cost can be separated from the node removal.
When the gate does not route, does the run still record the fused kernel's correctness, so that stage 5 can build on it?
